reviews.title: Stop guilt tripping people
reviews.body: There are a lot of really nice guided meditations on the app but I absolutely do not like the messages after meditations about keeping up my “streak” and there doesn’t seem to be any way to turn it off. I understand that some people may find them encouraging, but it just comes across as patronizing and hectoring to me. Which sort of defeats the point of meditation, doesn’t it?
this app is a waste of time. most of the meditation guidelines here are paid uneven the sound controls are locked in the free version.

reviews.title: Forced Questions
reviews.body:
I have been a user for a long time but the change to their revised, prescriptive meditation app that require numerous inputs prior to “letting” you just meditate, has turned me from a plus user to a non-paid to now avoiding it all together as it’s just frustrating.

Can you just let people do their meditation without shaming them into how many days it’s been or extracting how they currently feel just to fill your data needs? 

Just Stop.

reviews.title: This app is becoming unbearable...
reviews.body:
My friend and I were recently chatting, having a discussion on meditation and practices that we like. The subject of Insight Timer came up, I told her I liked it, and she said "yeah but isn't that the one that has so many prompts after the meditation and they make you commit to using it all the time?"

I just did a meditation and the amount of pop ups after is -there's no better way to put it - absolutely insane. I had to click through about 7 of them to get to the home screen. 

These prompts are an absolute deterrant for me to come back here and use the app more. Which is ironic, considering their begging me to continue using regularly. 

Insight timer is not my only meditation practice. I would like to be able to return, as I see fit, without being hounded. 

I'm tempted to delete the app.

Update: I'm deleting it. I opened the app and literally had to click through 15-20 answers before I could use the app. 

Absolute garbage.

reviews.title: Stop making me commit to streaks
reviews.body:
I’ve been using and loving Insight Timer for a long time. However, in the last year they have implemented some choices that have really not sat well with me. Primarily, it’s that they keep forcing me to ‘commit’ to streaks or how many days I’m going to meditate. This happens after sessions and sometimes when I load up the app. There’s no way to exit out of it - the app forces you to answer ‘how many days are you committing for?’ This isn’t cool. I’m not inviting or asking for the choice, and I either need to exit the app or make a choice on my commitment length that I don’t actually want to make and that’s not in integrity for me. 

It feels like they’re trying to force engagement and commitment. All they need to do is include a little X button to opt out of those screens. I don’t like feeling forced to put my word behind something that isn’t in integrity just to use the app.

They are constantly making changes to the app. And most not for good. More and more teachers' tracks are 'premium'. So it becomes less accessible if you have free. Too many tracks are metaphysical, psuedoscience under the guise of 'healing'. When you finish listening to a track, you have to click 4 or 5 times, including solicitation to review track, donate to teacher, etc. For an app that should be a simple, calming experience- this is aggravating, burdensome.

Every time I open this app, multiple times throughout the day, something has changed. The updates are incessant and keep moving things around, back and forth, making it more confusing. Some days I can't find my Saved stuff, or Teachers, and then some days they're all there. That's really the only two things I ask for on the home page. Stop moving things around!!

wayyyy too many pop ups for quotes/feedback/check-ins/streaks etc. too annoying and too slow too navigate. Would really like this app to get rid of unnecessary screens to tap on for those who don't want it.

Update 9/5/26: still can't open the app completely it starts then it closes itself. I can't get the app to open, it starts then closes immediately, I've updated to the latest version, I'm currently using my new phone a Pixel 11 Pro XL.
No thank you. the only thing that I need for meditation is a timer and a polite bell.

reviews.title: search is hopelessly broken
reviews.body: the search feature is nearly useless. search for a term, say, "stoicism," for example, and +1000 results will show in number.  Add a filter and the number drops impossibly low, and seemingly randomly, depending on when you search. I filtered by "talks" and returned only 51 results, and can only view 18 of them to choose from. Scrolling through +1000 results is not the meditative practice I was looking for, however, I am indeed, putting stoicism into practice and taking this in stride. This is not in my control, however, I may possibly influence it. Enough time spent on that.

reviews.title: WAS A must in this stage of my life.
reviews.body:
New review: I loved this app until it accidentally updated. I always intentionally avoid updates for various reasons, then wait until they work out inevitable bugs, but for all the newer features that are nice…there are a slew of issues that make this near useless for me. For instance… I built many playlists that I listen to often. I could stay in practice seamlessly, study for hours, fall asleep, whatever I chose. The screen would dim but the tracks would continue to play. Now, if the screen dims, or if I try to go dark to try and fall asleep, it illuminates after each track and stops so I have to hit play after every single track…what’s the point of wasting hours of time building playlists that don’t work and function like playlists???

The preview option is redundant and irritating and I see no way to turn it off. If I tapped a track before, it played 20-30 seconds of the track. That way I could tell if I liked the subject, voice, music, background, recording quality, etc. Now it goes to a different screen with a bunch of other tracks that have nothing in common with the one I want to just hear for a few seconds, and if I’m building a playlist it takes twice as long if I’m focusing on one teacher because I have to exit out of 2screens not just one and now it’s been over an hour of me trying to just meditate when I would’ve completed my nightly routine and been at calm, but it’s essentially useless. 

Who wants to snap out of meditation every 10-15, or even 30 minutes to hit play because now there are quadruple redundant steps to do what the old school system did flawlessly. I’m about to cancel my subscription, or..it could just be that instead of this being an easy lovely peaceful app like it has been the last few years for me, it’s turned into a nightmare. 

First review: Insight Timer has been incredibly helpful while going through difficulties, self reflection, or the little frustrations of everyday life. There are a vast variety of techniques, facilitators, subject matter, and other useful tools that are easily accessible, and for me, have proved to be invaluable. It didn’t take very long to figure out and find what I needed once I started using the app on a regular basis. It has become an integral part of my morning routine and I find myself going back to it more often throughout the day.

reviews.title: Starts at zero days practice every time it downloads an update!
reviews.body:
This app is good and I have recommended it to many people. However, it has a glitch and starts at zero days practice every time it downloads an update!
How can this be my first day using it when I’ve been using daily it for such a long time? Downloading an update for this application. Should not restart you at day one.

reviews.title: Bigger isn’t better
reviews.body: Still no way to mark the tracks or teachers I don’t like. Bigger isn’t better. Update: Did I just get a pop up about new live yoga right after I started my meditation timer? Yes. Yes, I did. Um, can’t the ads wait until after I’ve done my sitting practice? Updated review: some of the changes are good, but I think now that I've been using guided meditations more I've noticed places for improvement. First - it no longer switches to landscape view on the iPad - that's a small thing but it used to so now it's just frustrating. More importantly, to get to my bookmarked meditations, I have to go through something like 5 screens, many of them with very bright white backgrounds. In the dark morning this is very off putting. Finally, still, no download option means you have to be connected to the internet. I still love Insight Timer. The changes are great! One thing I would change: you can't rate a guided mediation unless you listen all the way thru. This means that 1)of course all the ratings are high bc who's going to sit thru 60 minutes of a bad mediation to rate it? and 2) there's no way to track those I've tried and didn't like. I wish there was some way to track negative ones as well as good ones. Older: This app has really helped me develop a meditation routine. Very dedicated customer service.

reviews.title: Lost its mission
reviews.body:
I’ve used Insight Timer for many years and have always appreciated what the app stood for: making meditation accessible to as many people as possible.

Unfortunately, over the last few years, it feels like the focus has shifted more toward monetization than accessibility. Features that were previously available with the free membership have gradually been removed or placed behind the paid subscription. I completely understand charging for premium content and features, but even some very basic sounds and options now require an upgrade.

What’s especially frustrating is the constant pop-ups encouraging you to upgrade while trying to use the free version. It makes the experience feel less peaceful and more like a sales funnel, which seems contrary to the purpose of a meditation app.

I don’t mind paying for a valuable service, but I wish Insight Timer would maintain a genuinely useful free experience while offering additional premium features for those who choose to upgrade. After being a longtime user, it’s disappointing to see the direction the app has taken.

I scrolled back through the history and now there are several holes in it. Not sure what gives there, but if I'm paying for an app/service, I expect it to function properly.

reviews.title: not worth it

reviews.body: While helpful in some areas, I really wish there was a way to filter out AI generated or assisted tracks.

reviews.title: Be mindful of where this is headed
reviews.body:
I am not excited about the new video update. This is a place we go to meditate and get away from social media. I appreciate the ability to follow  teachers that resonate with so we can see when they post new meditations. But I am bothered by the promotion of videos when I first open the app now, and what the addition of video format could mean for the direction of this app. 
It already is unpleasant to see the same, likely paid for, promoted teachers when I search for mediations. I don’t want to be advertised to and overstimulated by video clips trying to grab my attention. 
There’s enough content that’s been transitioned to subscriber only. 

Keep in mind the base intentions of the app.

reviews.body: I use to love this app. It was streamlined and easy to use. Now it’s cluttered with all kinds of roadblocks to getting started with questionnaires and dogma. It’s a huge turn off and I’m looking for a different app to use now. I’ve been on this app since 2014 and have seen it go downhill fast in the last few years.

reviews.title: Formerly excellent, now schlocky and gamified.
reviews.body:
I’ve used Insight Timer for about 10 years and paid for the subscription 4 of them. This past year, I’ve become very annoyed with it and I’m actually avoiding it. Despite paying for the premium, I am forced to encounter multiple popups and prompts just to meditate. 

No I don’t want to commit, journal, read random quotes, or tell the app my feelings. I don’t want to follow every teacher, notifications, or the widget. And there are so many meditations I am lost in the content and it’s hard to find what I need. Now it’s hard selling those expensive retreats. I’m going to cancel.

reviews.title: Too much work
reviews.body:
This app used to be very good but with all the new updates and features from the last few years since they updated the UI it became a disconnected mess. Sure there are good guided meditations but to find them it feels like you need to sift through a toxic bog that you will need to meditate to cleanse yourself from. The community used to feel connected but somehow the developers made it difficult to use and there is much less real interaction from the community. With all the clicks I need to shoo away before and after a meditation session I feel less grounded than before I even opened the app. 

If you’re looking for mindfulness you may find it here but at what cost?

reviews.title: There needs to me some tweaks
reviews.body:
This is a great app, and I’ve learned a lot from it. There’s a massive amount of content available, which I really appreciate. That said, there are a few things that I think would make the app significantly better:

1)Too many steps to get to the content I want. There are too many checkpoints and prompts when opening the app. I don’t think there needs to be a quote and questions every time I open it. I use Insight Timer specifically for anxiety and stress, and when I need the app, I’m often looking for something that will help me right away. Having to navigate through several screens before getting to the content I want can actually add more stress and anxiety.

2)There should be a “Skip Intro” button. I appreciate that many courses and meditations include longer introductions for people who are listening for the first time. However, if I’ve already heard the introduction, I should be able to skip it and get straight to the content.

3)Challenges and courses aren’t saving my progress/location. For some reason, the challenges and courses I’m currently working through aren’t staying easily accessible. Every day, I have to navigate through the app to find the challenge or course I’m working on. It would be much better if these were saved prominently so I could quickly pick up where I left off.

Overall, the content on Insight Timer is excellent, and I really value having so much of it available. The interface is good, but with these relatively simple tweaks, I think it could be WAY better and much easier to use especially for people who are turning to the app when they’re already stressed or anxious.
